phases.name: Read the frozen brief and expose assumptions
phases.description: Keep every supplied requirement, constraint, and hint visible; identify workload facts that must be learned before selecting a fleet size or parallelism topology.

phases.name: Place the admission, compute, and data components
phases.description: Add catalog-backed components for job admission and priority, elastic cluster control, run state, GPU workers, sharded input, distributed training, durable checkpoints, and observability.

phases.name: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
phases.description: Replay the accepted component actions into a connected interaction graph. The graph includes control feedback for queued work and recovery, so it describes a running platform rather than a one-shot DAG.

phases.name: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
phases.description: Make the distributed-training and failure-recovery tradeoffs explicit, then turn the supplied GPU, scaling, model-size, and recovery targets into measurements rather than unverified claims.

phases.name: Review the local architecture draft
phases.description: Summarize the design boundaries and the evidence still needed before any separate browser, AI, or publication review.

steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and expose assumptions
steps.title: Keep the verified problem wording intact
steps.content: FROZEN FACT — The problem is ‘Design a Distributed Model Training Platform’. Its description is: ‘Design a platform that enables distributed training of large ML models across multiple GPUs and nodes, handles data parallelism and model parallelism, and optimizes training throughput and cost.’ Requirements: ‘Support data-parallel and model-parallel training’; ‘Manage multi-node GPU clusters dynamically’; ‘Handle gradient synchronization across nodes’; ‘Implement checkpointing and fault tolerance’; ‘Optimize data loading to avoid GPU starvation’; ‘Support mixed-precision training’; ‘Track training metrics and resource utilization’; ‘Manage training job queues and priorities’. Constraints: ‘Linear scaling efficiency above 80%’; ‘Support training on 100+ GPUs’; ‘Recover from node failures within 5 minutes’; ‘GPU utilization above 85% during training’; ‘Support models up to 100B+ parameters’. Hints: ‘Use PyTorch FSDP or DeepSpeed for distributed training’; ‘Implement ZeRO optimization for memory efficiency’; ‘Use NCCL for high-performance GPU communication’; ‘Implement elastic training for dynamic cluster resizing’; ‘Use gradient compression for bandwidth optimization’; ‘Implement async checkpointing to avoid training pauses’. Hints are candidate techniques, not extra vendor mandates. These targets are acceptance criteria; this local review draft does not claim they have been met.

steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and expose assumptions
steps.title: Ask for the workload that determines the topology
steps.content: FACT — The brief supplies acceptance targets for scaling efficiency, a 100+ GPU fleet, node-failure recovery, GPU utilization, and model size. It does not specify model architecture, dataset size or format, sample or sequence lengths, job arrival profile, training duration, GPU SKU or memory, node count, interconnect bandwidth, storage/input throughput, queue-wait objective, budget, availability SLO, end-to-end throughput target, convergence deadline, or model-quality metric. ASSUMPTION — Any concrete hardware configuration, throughput number, SLO, or quality threshold beyond the stated targets is a design assumption until the workload owner confirms it. The recovery target's measurement start and end also need agreement. Do not infer a fixed topology or claim a target from the component diagram alone.

steps.phase: Read the frozen brief and expose assumptions
steps.title: Use hybrid parallelism only where profiling calls for it
steps.content: DESIGN CHOICE — Data parallelism replicates computation over different data shards and synchronizes gradients. For models whose state does not fit efficiently on each worker, FSDP or DeepSpeed ZeRO can shard parameters, gradients, and optimizer state; these are memory-efficient forms of data parallelism, not a substitute for every form of model parallelism. Add tensor or pipeline parallelism when the model architecture and memory profile require splitting layers or tensors across ranks. Confirm the hybrid topology with a representative model and measure communication overhead.

decision.question: How should the platform select data parallelism and model parallelism for a training job?
decision.chosen: Keep parallelism and process-group topology in the versioned job configuration; begin with sharded data parallelism where it fits, and add tensor or pipeline parallelism when model memory or measured throughput requires it.
decision.chosenReason: The brief requires both forms, while the right mix depends on model structure, memory, batch shape, and the GPU interconnect. A configurable hybrid avoids assuming one topology is best for every model.

alternatives.option: Use only replicated data parallelism for every model
alternatives.tradeoff: It is simple for smaller models but can exceed per-worker memory and increase synchronization cost for very large models.

alternatives.option: Use model parallelism for every training job
alternatives.tradeoff: It adds cross-device coordination even where independent data replicas would scale more simply.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Add the training job entry point
steps.content: ASSUMPTION — Provide a versioned API for a job specification that identifies the model and code revision, dataset manifest, resource request, parallelism configuration, precision mode, and priority. Validate the request and return a durable run identifier; the API should not wait for a long-running training job.

component.label: Training Job API
component.description: Validates versioned training specifications and durably admits jobs.
component.highlightReason: A durable run identity separates job submission from GPU execution.

properties.purpose: Validate the job specification and resource request, record the run identity, and enqueue accepted work without holding the request open for training.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Represent queued jobs and their priority
steps.content: FACT — Job queues and priorities are required. Persist queue state and make priority, resource class, and admission decisions visible; prevent a large GPU request from silently starving smaller eligible work. The fairness policy and preemption rules need workload-owner input.

component.label: Priority Training Queue
component.description: Durable queue for training jobs, priority metadata, and scheduling outcomes.
component.highlightReason: A queue absorbs bursty submissions and makes priority policy explicit.

properties.purpose: Keep accepted job references durable and expose priority, resource requirements, queue age, and retry state to the scheduler.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Schedule complete distributed jobs onto elastic capacity
steps.content: ASSUMPTION — Use a cluster scheduler to provision and resize worker groups. Treat the distributed ranks for a job as a coordinated gang: a partially placed group should wait or fail admission instead of starting collectives with missing ranks. Resize elastic jobs at a safe training boundary and preserve the job's recorded topology.

component.label: Elastic Training Scheduler
component.description: Coordinates job admission, gang placement, resource provisioning, and safe elastic resizing.
component.highlightReason: Gang placement and controlled resizing keep distributed ranks consistent.

properties.purpose: Consume priority and resource requirements, provision complete multi-node worker groups, and change membership only under the job's elastic-resize policy.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Keep job attempts and committed checkpoint references
steps.content: Store job identity, immutable configuration references, priority, attempt state, worker topology, and the pointer to the last fully committed checkpoint. The checkpoint bytes live in object storage; this store is control metadata and must not be mistaken for the checkpoint payload.

component.label: Run and Checkpoint Metadata
component.description: Durable job, attempt, priority, topology, and committed-manifest metadata.
component.highlightReason: Separating checkpoint references from checkpoint bytes makes recovery state inspectable.

properties.purpose: Persist run specifications, queue and attempt state, worker-group identity, and the manifest pointer only after all checkpoint shards are durable.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Add the multi-node GPU worker fleet
steps.content: FACT — The platform must manage multi-node GPU clusters dynamically and support training on 100+ GPUs. ASSUMPTION — GPU SKU and memory, node count and shape, accelerator interconnect, and available fleet inventory must be selected from the workload and benchmarked; the brief supplies none of those values and does not claim the capacity is already configured.

component.label: Elastic Multi-Node GPU Fleet
component.description: GPU worker nodes allocated to coordinated distributed training jobs.
component.highlightReason: The catalog GPU Cluster represents the multi-node accelerator capacity named by the brief.

properties.purpose: Supply scheduler-managed GPU nodes and the interconnect needed by distributed ranks; select accelerator and topology from measured job requirements rather than a fixed brief assumption.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Keep immutable dataset manifests and source data
steps.content: Use versioned dataset manifests and checksums so each run reads a stable input identity. Partitioning and storage format remain workload decisions; do not assume a specific provider, dataset size, or object layout from the brief.

component.label: Dataset and Shard Manifest Store
component.description: Versioned training inputs and manifests consumed by sharded data workers.
component.highlightReason: Stable manifests let data workers partition input without changing a run's dataset identity.

properties.purpose: Store source datasets and versioned shard manifests with integrity checks so each training attempt can identify the exact input it consumed.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Prefetch and shard training input
steps.content: Prepare balanced shards, parallel reads, bounded prefetch, and batched transforms near the training workers. Track input wait separately from compute and collective time; increase loader concurrency only when measurements show data starvation and available CPU, memory, storage, and network support it. Better-fed workers can contribute to the stated GPU-utilization target, but utilization is not useful training throughput, convergence, or model quality. No input-throughput number is specified; benchmark results are measurements, not brief-provided SLOs.

component.label: Sharded Input and Prefetch Workers
component.description: Autoscaled data workers that prepare balanced training batches and keep GPU ranks fed.
component.highlightReason: The catalog Processing Worker provides an editable data-processing role without inventing a new component type.

properties.purpose: Read assigned dataset shards, validate and transform samples, and prefetch bounded batches for the matching training ranks; expose input wait and backlog metrics.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Run the distributed training framework
steps.content: The training runtime owns rank setup, data and model parallel groups, optimizer state, mixed precision, and step-level metrics. Configure PyTorch FSDP or DeepSpeed/ZeRO as job-level choices; use NCCL collectives for cross-node gradient synchronization where supported by the selected hardware and framework. Runtime execution, allocated workers, and high step throughput do not establish convergence or final model quality; those require a model-specific validation metric and acceptance threshold, neither of which the brief specifies.

component.label: Distributed Training Runtime
component.description: Framework workers for hybrid parallelism, gradient collectives, mixed precision, and optimizer execution.
component.highlightReason: The catalog Model Training type is configured as Distributed and carries the framework-level training responsibilities.

properties.purpose: Run coordinated ranks with configured data, tensor, or pipeline parallelism; synchronize gradients across nodes, apply the selected mixed-precision mode, and emit step, memory, and communication measurements.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Store asynchronous checkpoint shards durably
steps.content: Write immutable checkpoint shards to object storage. A manifest is committed to run metadata only after every shard for the same logical training step has completed and passed integrity checks; incomplete uploads are not restart points.

component.label: Checkpoint and Model Artifact Store
component.description: Durable versioned storage for asynchronous distributed checkpoint shards and final artifacts.
component.highlightReason: Checkpoint bytes are persisted separately from the metadata that marks a complete recovery point.

properties.purpose: Persist immutable model, optimizer, random-state, and sampler checkpoint shards; expose versions and checksums so recovery can use only a complete manifest.

steps.phase: Place the admission, compute, and data components
steps.title: Observe utilization, step time, and queue health
steps.content: Collect GPU utilization and memory, input wait, step duration, collective duration, network throughput, checkpoint duration, queue age, worker placement, run cost, and failure-to-first-useful-step recovery duration. Record training loss separately from model-owner-selected validation metrics; neither GPU utilization nor throughput alone establishes convergence or quality. The brief gives no quality metric or threshold, so any numeric quality SLO is an assumption requiring approval. Alert on target misses and node loss, but report every supplied target as an unverified objective until measured.

component.label: Training and Fleet Observability
component.description: Job, GPU, data-pipeline, collective, checkpoint, and queue telemetry with actionable alerts.
component.highlightReason: Separate signals help attribute low GPU utilization to data, communication, placement, or checkpoint work.

properties.purpose: Correlate per-job throughput and GPU utilization with data wait, collective, queue, node, and checkpoint health so operators can diagnose target misses.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Enqueue accepted training jobs
steps.content: The API publishes a durable job reference and scheduling metadata; large payloads remain in versioned storage and are referenced by the job manifest.

connection.label: Accepted job and priority
connection.description: Durable job reference, priority, and resource request for scheduler admission.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Persist the submitted run identity
steps.content: Record the immutable job configuration reference—including the submitted priority—and initial attempt state before returning successful admission to the caller.

connection.label: Run specification and identity
connection.description: Versioned training configuration and durable run state.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Dispatch eligible jobs under priority policy
steps.content: The scheduler consumes queue order, priority, and requested resources while applying the agreed fairness and admission policy.

connection.label: Eligible jobs and priority
connection.description: Queue state and scheduling events consumed by the elastic cluster controller.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Give scheduling the durable recovery state
steps.content: The scheduler reads the job resource specification, attempt status, and last committed checkpoint reference before launching or restarting a worker group. This supplies inputs to the recovery path; scheduling or locating a checkpoint alone does not demonstrate that the end-to-end recovery objective is met.

connection.label: Resource request and recovery pointer
connection.description: Persisted job policy and only the most recently committed checkpoint manifest.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Place complete rank groups on GPU capacity
steps.content: Provision the coordinated worker group from the job's resource and topology request; apply elastic membership changes at a safe boundary. This is a scheduling and worker-capacity action only: placing ranks does not show that training converges or that the resulting model meets a quality criterion.

connection.label: Gang placement and resize policy
connection.description: Scheduler-managed allocation of all ranks and GPUs for a training attempt.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Scale data workers with the admitted job
steps.content: Allocate the sharded input workers from the same run identity so loader partitions and training ranks share a consistent dataset manifest.

connection.label: Run-scoped loader workers
connection.description: Resource placement and shard assignment for the job's input pipeline.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Read versioned shards into the prefetch pipeline
steps.content: Workers read only the manifest and shard assignments pinned by the run, validate input integrity, and prepare bounded batches.

connection.label: Pinned dataset shards
connection.description: Versioned input data and shard manifests consumed by data workers.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Feed batches to the matching distributed ranks
steps.content: Partition samples to avoid duplicated or imbalanced work across data-parallel ranks, and expose time blocked on input to the runtime. This can reduce input starvation and contribute to GPU utilization, but the utilization objective remains a measured resource target—not a convergence or model-quality result.

connection.label: Balanced prefetched batches
connection.description: Run-scoped batches and input-wait signals for the corresponding training ranks.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Launch framework ranks on allocated GPUs
steps.content: Bind each rank to its assigned accelerator and network topology. The training runtime forms process groups and coordinates collectives across the placed workers. Placement on 100+ GPUs exercises the fleet and communication path; rank allocation by itself does not prove convergence or model quality.

connection.label: Rank placement and collective fabric
connection.description: Allocated multi-node GPUs and interconnect used by data and model parallel training ranks.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Load the run configuration and restart reference
steps.content: Provide the exact training configuration and, on recovery, the committed checkpoint manifest to the newly placed worker group.

connection.label: Versioned run and resume state
connection.description: Training settings and the last fully committed checkpoint reference.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Upload checkpoint shards without blocking every step
steps.content: Capture a consistent logical step, transfer immutable shards asynchronously, and publish the complete manifest only after integrity checks succeed.

connection.label: Async checkpoint shard writes
connection.description: Consistent model, optimizer, random-state, and sampler shards written under an immutable checkpoint identity.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Commit attempt and checkpoint-manifest state
steps.content: After checkpoint storage confirms every shard, advance the metadata pointer atomically; also persist attempt completion or classified failure state.

connection.label: Attempt state and committed manifest
connection.description: Runtime outcome and the pointer to a checkpoint whose complete shard set is durable.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Restore only a complete checkpoint after worker loss
steps.content: A replacement worker group fetches the shards named by the last committed manifest and verifies them before resuming. Ignore partial uploads and retain the prior valid checkpoint until the new manifest is committed.

connection.label: Verified checkpoint restore
connection.description: Model and optimizer shards retrieved by a restarted training attempt from its committed manifest.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Publish step and collective measurements
steps.content: Export step time, examples or tokens processed, training loss, and (when defined by the model owner) validation metrics, plus memory, input wait, collective duration, checkpoint overhead, and run outcome with run and topology identity. Throughput and training loss are useful diagnostics, but neither alone establishes convergence or final model quality; the brief supplies no validation metric or threshold.

connection.label: Training step and communication metrics
connection.description: Per-run metrics for throughput, GPU use, memory, input stalls, collectives, and checkpoint overhead.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Export node and accelerator utilization
steps.content: Correlate per-device utilization, memory pressure, node health, and interconnect counters with the ranks and job that own them.

connection.label: GPU, node, and fabric health
connection.description: Hardware utilization and failure signals tagged by worker, rank, and training attempt.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Measure placement and elastic resize outcomes
steps.content: Record pending resource requests, gang placement delay, worker replacement, and resize events so low utilization can be separated from scheduling delay.

connection.label: Placement and resize events
connection.description: Resource waits, gang scheduling, worker replacement, and elastic membership changes.

steps.phase: Connect training, checkpoint, and telemetry paths
steps.title: Expose queue age and priority outcomes
steps.content: Track queue age and admitted work by priority and resource class; use this to distinguish capacity shortage from a deliberate admission or fairness decision.

connection.label: Queue age and priority state
connection.description: Queue depth, oldest eligible work, resource class, and scheduling outcome.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Make priority and preemption behavior explicit
steps.content: DESIGN CHOICE — Use an explicit policy such as weighted fair admission across teams and resource classes, with priority overrides governed by the platform owner. Preempt a running job only when its checkpoint and restart cost are understood; never assume priority means arbitrary interruption.

decision.question: How should high-priority jobs use scarce multi-node GPU capacity?
decision.chosen: Keep priority and resource requirements in durable queue state, apply a documented fairness policy, and preempt only through a checkpoint-aware policy approved for the workload.
decision.chosenReason: This preserves priority ordering while making starvation, queue age, and recovery cost observable and reviewable.

alternatives.option: Always run the highest-priority job immediately
alternatives.tradeoff: Can starve lower-priority work and fragment multi-node capacity.
Protects active work but may leave urgent jobs waiting behind long runs.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Measure support at the stated fleet scale
steps.content: FACT — The fleet-capacity target is training on 100+ GPUs. Validate that a representative job can be admitted, placed across the requested ranks, and kept healthy at that scale; separately measure collective behavior and throughput. This gate demonstrates scheduling and worker capacity only: it does not prove model convergence or acceptable model quality, and a GPU Cluster component label is not evidence that the target has been achieved.

scaleTrigger.metric: Admitted and healthy training ranks across a representative run using 100+ GPUs
scaleTrigger.action: If complete worker groups cannot be placed or sustained, inspect queue admission, available accelerator inventory, topology constraints, collective errors, and network saturation before changing the parallelism plan.
scaleTrigger.impact: Tests the stated capacity as an end-to-end job outcome instead of counting provisioned devices alone.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Choose gradient synchronization from the worker topology
steps.content: DESIGN CHOICE — Use framework-managed NCCL collectives for gradient synchronization on supported GPU paths. Select process groups and hierarchical communication from the actual node and fabric topology. Evaluate gradient compression only when communication is the measured bottleneck; compare compressed and uncompressed runs with the same workload and an owner-approved convergence and validation-quality criterion. The brief provides no such quality threshold, so do not invent one.

decision.question: How should ranks synchronize gradients without hiding communication bottlenecks?
decision.chosen: Use NCCL all-reduce or reduce-scatter/all-gather as required by the selected parallelism strategy, expose collective duration and bytes, and enable compression only after a representative quality and throughput comparison.
decision.chosenReason: Collective choice follows the sharding strategy and hardware topology; conditional compression avoids trading model quality for an unverified bandwidth gain.

alternatives.tradeoff: Can change convergence or add encode/decode work when communication is not the limiting factor.

alternatives.option: Treat gradient exchange as local to each node
alternatives.tradeoff: Does not synchronize replicas across the multi-node worker group.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Find input starvation before adding GPU capacity
steps.content: FACT — The brief sets GPU utilization above 85% during training. Measure utilization alongside input wait, step time, collective time, and data-worker backlog. Do not attribute every idle GPU to insufficient GPU count; input stalls and synchronization can dominate. Utilization is a resource-efficiency signal, not proof of useful throughput, convergence, or model quality; no separate numeric throughput objective is stated.

scaleTrigger.metric: Per-job GPU utilization against the stated above-85% target, correlated with input wait, collective duration, and data-worker backlog
scaleTrigger.action: If utilization is below target and input wait is material, profile shard balance, read throughput, transforms, and bounded prefetch; if collective time dominates, inspect rank balance, process groups, and fabric counters.
scaleTrigger.impact: Directs optimization toward the measured starvation source and avoids scaling an already idle accelerator fleet.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Select mixed precision with numerical checks
steps.content: FACT — Mixed-precision training is required. ASSUMPTION — The framework and selected accelerator expose a job-level precision mode and supported numeric formats. Validate loss stability, overflow behavior, optimizer state, convergence, and final quality for the model; use higher-precision accumulation where required by the framework and workload. The brief does not define a convergence or quality metric/threshold, so agree it with the model owner rather than treating capacity or speed as a substitute.

decision.question: How should a job choose a mixed-precision mode without masking numerical regressions?
decision.chosen: Version the precision mode with the run configuration, validate it on representative training data, and retain the precision and scaler state needed for a consistent checkpoint resume.
decision.chosenReason: A recorded mode makes throughput comparisons reproducible while numerical checks protect training correctness.

alternatives.option: Force one precision mode for every model
alternatives.tradeoff: Can reduce stability or miss a faster safe mode for a particular architecture and accelerator.

alternatives.option: Change precision during a run without recording it
alternatives.tradeoff: Makes reproduction and checkpoint continuation ambiguous.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Make checkpoint commits atomic across ranks
steps.content: DESIGN CHOICE — Coordinate a consistent logical step across ranks, snapshot model and optimizer shards plus random and sampler state, then write immutable objects asynchronously. Publish a new manifest only after every shard is durable and checksum-verified. Keep the prior complete manifest available until that commit succeeds.

decision.question: What state must be durable before a restarted distributed job can safely resume?
decision.chosen: Commit a versioned all-rank checkpoint manifest after model, optimizer, precision-scaler, random-state, and data-sampler state have been written and verified for the same logical step.
decision.chosenReason: A committed manifest prevents recovery from mixing rank shards or resuming data and optimizer state from different steps.

alternatives.option: Update the latest pointer before all shard writes finish
alternatives.tradeoff: A node failure can leave the pointer referencing an incomplete checkpoint.

alternatives.option: Block training until every checkpoint upload finishes
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies ordering but adds checkpoint storage latency directly to the training critical path.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Budget the complete five-minute recovery path
steps.content: FACT — The stated recovery objective is to recover from node failures within five minutes. Measure from detected node loss to the first useful resumed training step, including failure detection, rank-group teardown, replacement capacity, checkpoint lookup and transfer, process-group formation, and input restoration. The design does not claim this target is achieved.

scaleTrigger.metric: Detected node failure to first useful optimizer step after resume; stated objective: within five minutes
scaleTrigger.action: If recovery exceeds the objective, identify whether detection, GPU placement, checkpoint transfer, integrity validation, or collective reformation consumed the budget; retain the prior checkpoint and make restart operations idempotent.
scaleTrigger.impact: Measures end-to-end recovery rather than only worker replacement or checkpoint-read time.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Benchmark the stated linear scaling efficiency
steps.content: FACT — The target is linear scaling efficiency above 80%. Compare measured useful throughput for a fixed representative workload across worker counts, holding data, effective-batch semantics, precision, and training work constant; report the baseline, parallelism configuration, and communication share. The brief specifies no absolute examples-per-second or tokens-per-second target. Higher scaling efficiency means the fixed work is delivered more efficiently; it does not by itself show faster convergence or better model quality. If comparing time to a quality milestone, use a separately agreed validation metric and threshold.

scaleTrigger.metric: Strong-scaling efficiency for the same workload against the stated above-80% objective
scaleTrigger.action: When measured efficiency misses the objective, decompose step time into compute, input, synchronization, and checkpoint work; then test topology, shard balance, batch policy, or communication changes one at a time.
scaleTrigger.impact: Makes the scaling constraint reproducible and directs work to the actual source of lost parallel efficiency.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Validate the 100B-plus model envelope
steps.content: FACT — The platform must support models up to 100B+ parameters. Exercise representative model state, optimizer state, activations, sequence or batch shape, checkpoint shards, and restore behavior at the stated envelope. Parameter count by itself does not determine the memory or throughput requirement. Passing this fit/train/checkpoint/restore capacity test does not establish convergence or final model quality; assess those separately against an owner-approved metric, which the brief leaves unspecified.

scaleTrigger.metric: Successful train, checkpoint, and restore for a representative model at the stated 100B+ parameter envelope
scaleTrigger.action: If memory or communication blocks the run, profile model-state, optimizer, activation, and checkpoint footprints; validate sharded data parallelism and add tensor or pipeline parallelism where the model structure warrants it.
scaleTrigger.impact: Connects the model-size constraint to actual peak memory, communication, and recovery behavior.

steps.phase: Choose parallelism, recovery, and throughput policies
steps.title: Balance elastic capacity against interruption cost
steps.content: DESIGN CHOICE — Scale worker capacity from queued demand and measured job needs, but resize a running distributed group only when the framework supports an agreed safe transition. Treat the stated 100+ GPU fleet and above-85% utilization as separate acceptance targets to measure, not resize guarantees. Compare idle GPU cost with queue delay and checkpoint/restart cost; the brief supplies no budget, queue-wait SLO, or service-level policy, so those weights remain owner decisions. GPU count and utilization govern capacity planning; neither is a proxy for convergence or model quality.

decision.question: When should the scheduler resize a running training job or hold capacity for queued work?
decision.chosen: Use explicit admission and elastic-resize policies based on queue age, resource availability, measured throughput, and checkpoint safety; expose the cost and delay signals for policy review.
decision.chosenReason: Dynamic capacity can improve utilization and queue responsiveness, but uncontrolled resizing can disrupt collectives, waste checkpoint work, or make performance unstable.

alternatives.option: Keep every GPU allocation fixed for the full job
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids resize transitions but may hold scarce capacity while work is queued or input-starved.

alternatives.option: Resize worker membership continuously from instantaneous utilization
alternatives.tradeoff: Can churn distributed ranks and react to short-lived signals rather than useful job throughput.

steps.phase: Review the local architecture draft
steps.title: Review the design and remaining evidence
steps.content: LOCAL REVIEW DRAFT — The architecture connects durable job admission and priority scheduling to elastic multi-node GPU placement, sharded input, a distributed training runtime, verified asynchronous checkpoints, restart metadata, and correlated telemetry. Its main choices are configurable hybrid parallelism, measured NCCL communication, checkpoint-aware recovery, and bottleneck-led throughput tuning. The supplied targets remain unverified acceptance criteria. Browser persistence, AI assessment, and publication gates are separate and have not been run or passed by this local draft.
